rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: a sacrifice is giving up material on purpose to win something bigger. A combination is a series of forcing moves, with a sacrifice, that ends in a gain.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess. The black rook on b2 is in your camp, defended by the bishop on g7 along the long diagonal.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.p: Find the sacrifice with check that prepares a second blow.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes: the rook captures the pawn on h7 with check. The bishop on b3 controls g8, so the king can only escape by capturing the rook.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.revela: The sacrifice is the rook capturing the pawn on h7 with check: the king can only take it, because the bishop on b3 controls g8.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2c3.1: The bishop goes to c3 and attacks the rook on b2, but the bishop on g7 also reaches c3 along the long diagonal.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2c3.2: With this move Black captures the bishop for free, and the rook on b2 stays in your camp.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2c3.3: Back to the position: look for a sacrifice with check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2b4.1: The bishop goes to b4 and attacks the rook on f8, but it gives no check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2b4.2: The rook goes to f7 on purpose: if the bishop on b3 takes it, the rook on b2 gives your king check after check, and the game ends in a draw. The win is gone.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2b4.3: Back to the position: look for a sacrifice with check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2h6.1: The bishop goes to h6 and offers a bishop trade, but it gives no check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2h6.2: With this move, the rook on b2 captures the pawn on g2, and Black wins material.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.d2h6.3: Back to the position: look for a sacrifice with check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.semXeque: This move gives no check, and the rook on b2 stays in your camp, defended by the bishop on g7. Black gains time to attack your king.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.err.semXeque.vol: Back to the position: look for a sacrifice with check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not prepare a second blow. Look for a sacrifice with check to the black king.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the sacrifice.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.1: With the check, the king can neither stay on h8 nor run to g8: it has to capture the rook.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.2: The king captures the rook and goes to h7. This is attraction: now the king is on the h-file, within reach of the other rook.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.3: Second blow: the other rook goes to h1 with check. The king has no square to run to, and Black must block the check.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.4: The bishop on g7 blocks the check, but it leaves the long diagonal, and the rook on b2 is left undefended. This is deflection.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.5: The rook captures the bishop on h6 with check, defended by the bishop on d2.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.6: The king steps out of check to g7 and attacks the rook on h6, but the rook on b2 is still undefended.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.7: The white king captures the rook on b2. White gave up a rook and got back a rook, a bishop and a pawn.
rot.twoMotifs.ideia.ex1.l.8: In positions like this, the combination works because the sacrifice prepares the second blow. Without the check on h1, the rook given up would just be lost material.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. This is the Game of the Century: Game Donald Byrne vs Bobby Fischer, Rosenwald Memorial, New York 1956. The black queen on b6 is attacked by the bishop on c5.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.1: The first motif is the queen sacrifice: Fischer does not save it. The bishop on g4 goes to e6 and attacks the bishop on c4, and taking on c4 will come with check to the king on f1.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.2: Byrne accepts the sacrifice and captures the queen on b6. Declining would also have lost material for White.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.3: The bishop captures on c4 with check. The second motif begins, a series of checks by the bishop and the knight.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.4: The king steps out of check to g1.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.5: The knight goes to e2 and gives check, and f1 is the king's only square.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.6: The king goes back to f1, the only square it has.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.fischer.l.7: The knight captures the pawn on d4 and uncovers the check from the bishop on c4. With this series of checks, Fischer won pieces for the queen and went on to win the game.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.1: Attack: back to White. Game Réti vs Tartakower, Vienna 1910, from a Caro-Kann. The rook on d1 stands behind the bishop and the queen.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.l.1: The queen sacrifices itself on d8 with check. The rook on d1 does not defend it yet, because the bishop on d2 is in the way.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.l.2: The king is forced to capture the queen, because it has no other square. This is attraction: the king goes to d8, on the rook's file.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.l.3: The bishop leaves d2 and gives check from g5, and the rook on d1 also gives check along the open file. It is a double check.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.l.4: The king runs to c7: in a double check only the king can move. On e8, the rook would mate on d8.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.reti.l.5: The bishop goes to d8 and gives mate. In positions like this, the queen given up was worth it because it cleared the way for the double check.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.1: Attack: still White. Game knightking64 vs Ogloblin, Lichess 2021, between two masters. The black queen on f4 and the king on f8 are on the f-file, and only the pawn on f7 separates them.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.1: The knight sacrifices itself on e6: it captures the pawn with check and attacks the queen on f4. If the king steps out of check, the knight takes the queen.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.2: The pawn on f7 recaptures the knight and leaves the f-file. This is the first motif: the recapture opens the line between the queen and the king.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.3: Second blow: the rook goes to f1 and pins the queen on f4 against the king on f8.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.4: The pawn on g6 goes to g5 and defends the queen, but it stays pinned. Giving up the queen for the rook on f1 also lost.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.5: The rook captures the queen with check.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.abreLinha.l.6: The pawn recaptures the rook. White gave up the knight and the rook and won the queen: in positions like this, the forced recapture opens the line for the second blow.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.1: Attack: still White. Game wohen1 vs FrustratedNoob, Lichess 2023, from a Caro-Kann. The bishop on g3 attacks the white queen on h4, and there are two sacrifices with check, on h7 and on f6.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.l.1: First the sacrifice on h7: the bishop captures the pawn with check, to bring the king onto the h-file.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.l.2: The knight on f6 captures the bishop, and the queen on h4 is still attacked. White gave up the bishop with no second blow.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.volta: Back to the position: before the sacrifice, check whether the position allows the second blow. Here the knight on f6 defends h7.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.c.1: Now the sacrifice on f6: the knight captures the defender of h7 with check, and Black has no time to take the queen. This is removing the defender.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.c.2: The pawn on g7 recaptures the knight. If the king went to h8, the mate would be the same.
rot.twoMotifs.demos.excecao.c.3: The queen captures on h7, defended by the bishop on d3, and gives mate. In positions like this, the sacrifice works only with the second blow calculated to the end.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: There are two sacrifices on f7, with the rook and with the bishop. Does it work here? Check which one prepares a second blow and play as White.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The right sacrifice was the rook's: after the recapture, the rook on f7 was pinned by the bishop on b3, and the queen captured the pawn on g6 with check.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.valeAqui.err.b3f7: With the bishop, the rook on f8 recaptures and nothing is pinned: you just give up the bishop. Look for the sacrifice that leaves a black piece pinned.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.valeAqui.err.sai: The rook steps away from the pawn on g6, but the chance is gone. One of the sacrifices on f7 prepares a second blow.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.valeAqui.err.b3f7b: The bishop captures the rook with check, but the queen recaptures, and the pin is gone. With the rook on f7 pinned, the queen can capture the pawn on g6 with check.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.descoberto.enuncia: Now let us think from Black's side. Your bishop on d7 stands between your queen and the white queen. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.descoberto.fim: The rook captured the bishop on e2 with check and drew the king to e2. Then the bishop left d7 with check, and your queen began attacking the white queen.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.descoberto.err.d7b: The bishop moves and uncovers the attack, but without check: the queen on e7 takes your queen first. Look for a sacrifice that lets the bishop move with check.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.descoberto.err.out: After this move, the white queen stays free to attack your king. There is a blow that uses the bishop on d7.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.descoberto.err.pas: After this move, the white queen escapes. The white king went to e2: look for the bishop move that gives check.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.retira: The queen is saved, but there is a stronger sacrifice that opens the e-file for the rook on e1.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.enunciado: Back to White. The bishop on f5 attacks your queen, and the pawn on e6 closes the e-file. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.fim: The queen captured the bishop on f5, and the pawn on e6 recaptured and opened the e-file. Then the knight left e5 with a discovered check from the rook and attacked the queen on b6.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.e5c6: The knight captures on c6, but your queen is still attacked, and the bishop on f5 takes it.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.e5d7: The knight attacks the queen on b6, but the king takes it, and your queen is still attacked.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.e5g6: The knight uncovers the rook's check, but on g6 it does not attack the queen on b6. The king steps out of check, and you gave up the queen for a bishop.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.e5c6b: The knight uncovers the rook's check, but on c6 it does not attack the queen on b6. The king steps out of check, and you gave up the queen for a bishop.
rot.twoMotifs.pratica.colunaE.err.e5d7b: The knight uncovers the check and attacks the queen on b6, but on d7 the king takes it.
